response:
Pointwise convergence of a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) to f(x) on [0, 1] does not necessarily imply uniform convergence.

Consider the sequence of polynomials B_n(x) = x^n. This sequence converges pointwise to f(x) = 0 on [0, 1), but not uniformly. In fact, the sequence converges uniformly to f(x) = 0 on [0, 1) but not on [0, 1].

To see this, note that for any fixed x in [0, 1), the sequence B_n(x) = x^n converges to 0 as n approaches infinity. However, the sequence does not converge uniformly on [0, 1) because the rate of convergence depends on x. Specifically, for x = 1, the sequence B_n(1) = 1^n = 1 for all n, so it does not converge to 0.

In contrast, the sequence B_n(x) = x^n converges uniformly to 0 on [0, 1) because the supremum of |B_n(x) - f(x)| = |x^n| is bounded by 1 for all x in [0, 1).

Therefore, pointwise convergence of a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) to f(x) on [0, 1] does not necessarily imply uniform convergence.
